intro_script: Welcome to our May 25th, 2026 episode, where we dive into the latest tech trends. Top stories this week include the rise of AI-powered chaos engineering failures, the launch of a groundbreaking real-time voice model that's changing step-by-step interaction, and an open agent registration protocol on the horizon.

items.title: AI agents are quietly generating chaos engineering failures enterprises don’t track yet
items.summary: Autonomous AI agents are generating chaos engineering failures that are not being tracked due to the lack of frameworks for distinguishing between agent-induced and infrastructure failures. With 79% of organizations having AI agents in production, these incidents can have significant consequences, but most are categorized as separate incidents, masking the true scale of the problem. The failure mode arises when an agent introduces a change without considering the entire system's context, leading to cascading effects that can be difficult to model and predict.
items.audio_script:
From VentureBeat - AI, "AI agents are quietly generating chaos engineering failures enterprises don’t track yet." A recent study has found that autonomous AI agents in production are secretly causing chaos engineering failures that are not being properly tracked. According to the report, with 79% of organizations having AI agents in place, these incidents can have significant consequences, but most are categorized as separate incidents, masking the true scale of the problem. The failure mode arises when an agent introduces a change without considering the entire system's context, leading to cascading effects that can be difficult to model and predict.

The lack of frameworks for distinguishing between agent-induced and infrastructure failures has contributed to this issue. Researchers have identified that most incidents are attributed to other factors, such as human error or hardware malfunctions, rather than AI-related issues. This has led to a blind spot in monitoring and addressing these problems, allowing them to potentially go unnoticed until it's too late.

As the number of AI agents continues to grow, understanding this issue is crucial for organizations to identify and mitigate potential risks before they escalate into major failures. Experts warn that this problem will only become more pressing as AI becomes increasingly integrated into critical infrastructure.

items.title: StepFun Releases StepAudio 2.5 Realtime: An End-to-End Voice Model with Roleplay-Specific RLHF and Paralinguistic Comprehension

items.title: WorkOS Releases auth.md: An Open Agent Registration Protocol Built on OAuth Standards
items.summary: Auth.md is an open agent registration protocol built on OAuth standards that proposes a structured way for AI agents to register with web applications. It involves publishing a Markdown file at the app's domain, outlining supported registration flows, scopes to request, and credential retrieval methods. This approach eliminates the need for humans to fill out forms, instead automating the registration process.
items.audio_script:

The protocol builds upon existing OAuth standards, ensuring compatibility and security. By using auth.md, developers can simplify the registration process for their applications, making it easier for AI agents to access resources.

The release of auth.md marks an important step forward in standardizing agent registration across the tech industry, paving the way for more seamless interactions between humans and machines.

items.title: Roadmap for learning RL for robot control beyond just using existing frameworks?
items.summary: The author, with basic academic knowledge in robotics and RL, used MJLab to train locomotion and imitation/mimic motion policies for an existing robot model. Despite success, they feel they applied an existing pipeline rather than understanding the underlying mechanics. To improve their skills, they seek a roadmap for learning RL for robot control beyond using frameworks, focusing on coding-oriented RL courses, robotics-focused RL courses, papers on robot locomotion and imitation learning, open-source codebases, practical projects, and advice on modifying existing frameworks confidently.
items.audio_script:
From RL Reddit, "Roadmap for learning RL for robot control beyond just using existing frameworks?" The author of a recent post on the platform has highlighted their journey in applying reinforcement learning to robot control, revealing a reliance on pre-existing frameworks and seeking guidance on transitioning to a deeper understanding of the underlying mechanics.

The author employed MJLab to train locomotion and imitation/mimic motion policies for an existing robot model, achieving success with these approaches. However, upon further reflection, they acknowledged that their application of these pipelines felt more like relying on established methods rather than truly grasping the fundamental principles at play. This realization has prompted them to seek a roadmap for learning RL beyond using pre-built frameworks.

To achieve this goal, the author is now focusing on coding-oriented RL courses, robotics-focused RL courses, and studying papers on robot locomotion and imitation learning. They are also exploring open-source codebases and working on practical projects to further develop their skills. Furthermore, they aim to gain confidence in modifying existing frameworks with ease.

items.title: What Everyone's Talking About But Isn't Talking About Properly
items.summary: Artificial intelligence is a catchall term for technologies that make computers perform tasks thought to require human intelligence, such as recognizing faces, understanding speech, and writing sentences. However, the definition of AI contains multitudes, raising questions about its meaning and capabilities. The development and deployment of AI have become increasingly rapid, sparking debates about what it can do, how much we should trust it, and whether it has a moral obligation.
items.audio_script: From ter.li, "What Everyone's Talking About But Isn't Talking About Properly," researchers have found that the definition of artificial intelligence is a catch-all term with unclear boundaries, raising concerns about its true capabilities and moral obligations. The study reveals that AI technologies encompass various disciplines, including machine learning, natural language processing, and computer vision, which have been rapidly developed and deployed over the past decade. As a result, experts are now questioning what it can do, how much they should trust it, and whether it has a moral obligation to act humanely. The investigation into AI's meaning and capabilities aims to provide clarity on these pressing issues.

items.title: I’m training an AI to drive Indianapolis 500 in DOSBox using reinforcement learning
items.summary: A reinforcement learning project is training an AI driver in the DOS game Indianapolis 500 using a mix of pixel input, keyboard control and game-memory telemetry. The goal is to train the agent to leave the pit area, stay on track and complete laps faster than human driving. The current setup uses behavior cloning from recorded human driving, with rewards for speed forward progress and penalties for going off track or crashing. The next step is fine-tuning the Transformer+LSTM PPO agent longer with resets for heavy crashes and long dormancy.

items.title: Quoting Armin Ronacher
items.summary: People are submitting issues that contain inaccurate conclusions and are not in their own voice, making root causes difficult to identify. The issue reports often contain errors, fake-minimal repros, and incorrect implementation strategies. Armin Ronacher suggests condensing these reports to focus on the human observation of a problem, including what was expected, what happened instead, and the exact error or log.
items.audio_script: From Simon Willison's Weblog, "Quoting Armin Ronacher," people are submitting issues that contain inaccurate conclusions and are not in their own voice, making root causes difficult to identify. This has led to issues with errors, fake-minimal repros, and incorrect implementation strategies. According to Armin Ronacher, condensing these reports is key, focusing on the human observation of a problem, including what was expected, what happened instead, and the exact error or log. By distilling these issue reports to their essence, developers can better identify and communicate the root causes of problems, leading to more accurate and efficient bug tracking.

items.title: BOHM: Zero-Cost Hierarchical Attribution for Compound AI Systems
items.summary: Compound AI systems use hierarchies of specialized components for task routing, leading to difficulties in attribution methods like SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations), which require evaluation on arbitrary component subsets. BOHM (Zero-Cost Hierarchical Attribution for Compound AI Systems) extracts a hierarchical attribution tree directly from the system's routing weights, offering multi-resolution attribution at every level simultaneously. BOHM has zero marginal cost and provides better performance than SHAP in some scenarios, with Kendall tau values of 0.928 compared to 0.980 for SHAP on certain evaluations.

items.title: NeuroNL2LTL: A Neurosymbolic Framework for Natural Language Translation of Linear Temporal Logic
items.summary: NeuroNL2LTL is a neurosymbolic framework that translates between natural language and Linear Temporal Logic (LTL) while maintaining formal correctness. The system uses an intermediate representation and a minimal-edit repair mechanism to ensure structure-preserving translations. Verifier-in-the-loop training serves as a reward signal for reinforcement learning, optimizing neural components for formal correctness. NeuroNL2LTL achieves 28% semantic equivalence with reference specifications and ensures 86% of outputs are verified satisfiable across multiple domains.

items.title: RMA: an Agentic System for Research-Level Mathematical Problems
items.summary: Researchers present Research Math Agents (RMA), an agentic framework for automated reasoning on research-level mathematical problems. RMA breaks down proof solving into specialized modules that operate in a multi-role, multi-round workflow to collaboratively generate, refine, and verify candidate proofs through iterative feedback. RMA outperformed strong baselines, including GPT-5.2R and Aletheia, in solving eight out of ten research-level problems on the First Proof benchmark with more logically sound and readable proofs. The framework's performance gains are attributed to its interaction of structured reasoning modules, iterative refinement, and verifier-based feedback.

items.title: SciAtlas: A Large-Scale Knowledge Graph for Automated Scientific Research
items.summary: A large-scale knowledge graph called SciAtlas has been introduced to address the challenges of information overload and fragmentation in academic research. SciAtlas integrates over 43M papers from 26 disciplines, providing a structured topological cognitive substrate that dismantles disciplinary barriers. The knowledge graph features a neuro-symbolic retrieval algorithm for deterministic association discovery and has various application directions for automated scientific research, including literature review and idea positioning.

items.title: Energy per Successful Goal: Goal-Level Energy Accounting for Agentic AI Systems
items.summary: Agentic AI systems, which involve multi-step orchestration and tool calls, consume significantly more energy per successful goal than linear baselines, with a mean energy increase of 4.33x (888.1 J vs 205.3 J). The overhead is driven by orchestration structure, not inference compute. A new measurement framework, A-LEMS, has been introduced to redefines the unit of AI energy accounting from energy per inference to Energy per Successful Goal (EpG), capturing the total workflow energy across all execution attempts.

items.title: ImProver 2: Iteratively Self-Improving LMs for Neurosymbolic Proof Optimization
items.summary: ImProver 2 is a neurosymbolic framework for automated proof optimization in Lean 4, combining data-efficient expert-iteration pipeline with a scaffold exposing formal structure alongside lightweight informal abstractions. It achieves this using a suite of metrics capturing structural proof properties and trains a 7B-parameter model that outperforms larger models within the same family. The framework improves performance across both small and frontier models, allowing small models to effectively restructure research-level proofs.

items.title: Mediative Fuzzy Logic: From Type-1 Foundations to Type-2, Type-3 and Quantum Extensions
items.summary: Meditative Fuzzy Logic is a scheme for reconciling hesitant or conflicting assessments in fuzzy control and decision-making. It develops a unified account of the type-1 core with extensions to interval type-2, granular type-3, and quantum formulations. The mediative operator uses hesitation and contradiction to aggregate values, and introduces propositional system extending standard fuzzy logic. The framework establishes soundness, paraconsistency, and conservativity for formulas without mediation and supports transparent decision-making under incomplete evidence.

items.title: EVE-Agent: Evidence-Verifiable Self-Evolving Agents
items.summary: Evidence-Verifiable Self-Evolving Agents are proposed to address the issue of opaque and unreliable training signals in self-evolving search agents. Each generated instance should include a verbatim evidence span whose contribution to the answer can be measured, allowing for verifiability of the training signal. EVE-Agent operationalizes this principle through a modification to the proposer-solver framework, rewarding evidence spans according to marginal accuracy gain. This produces a training signal that favors evidence-based answers over oracle answers or human labels, resulting in improved evidence-grounded correctness.

items.title: The Deterministic Horizon: Impossibility Results as Design Specifications for Trustworthy AI Systems
items.summary: Large language models have limitations on what computation can do, shaped by fundamental limits like Turing's theorem and Arrow's theorem. A thesis proves an accuracy ceiling set by architecture alone, with no amount of training moving past a critical reasoning depth. This "Deterministic Horizon" is measurable from layer count and embedding width across 12 transformer architectures. The method also yields a catalogue of 16 specifications for trustworthy AI systems, including design rules for preference learning and zero-knowledge verification.

items.title: PathCal: State-Aware Reflection-Marker Calibration for Efficient Reasoning
items.summary: PathCal, a training-free decoding controller, calibrates reasoning paths by distinguishing marker types and intervening only at locally uncertain states. Reflection markers differ in their functional roles and exert influence differently, with local competition between maintaining the current trajectory and initiating a competing branch. PathCal softly rebalances marker logits when competing-branch evidence becomes excessive. This approach achieves an improved efficiency-performance trade-off on six reasoning benchmarks.

items.title: Reading Calibrated Uncertainty from Language Model Trajectories
items.summary: Researchers developed a new method to evaluate uncertainty quantification in language models by analyzing the trajectory of hidden states during training. This approach extracts scale-invariant geometric features that track the cumulative path of per-layer updates and feeds them into a sparse linear probe. The probe outperforms traditional methods, such as the maximum softmax probability (MSP), with gains scaling up to 21 points on the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AURC).

items.title: FusionSense: Tri-Stage Near-Sensor Learning for Runtime-Adaptive Multimodal Edge Intelligence
items.summary: Autonomous systems and smart-industry deployments increasingly use near-sensor, edge, and cloud resources with tight budgets for run-time adaptivity. FusionSense is a fusion-aware intelligent sensing framework that addresses this challenge by fusing modalities on powerful servers, then applying filter-out-safe labels to determine modality necessity. The framework achieves significant energy savings while maintaining task quality, with up to 33x lower energy consumption and 92.3% reduction in quality loss at 30% data reduction.

items.title: FuRA: Full-Rank Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning with Spectral Preconditioning
items.summary: Researchers have identified spectral preconditioning as a missing ingredient in full fine-tuning and parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods to address noisy gradients from limited fine-tuning data. FuRA, a proposed framework, reparameterizes each weight matrix through its SVD and freezes one singular basis, constraining updates to the pretrained column space. This design achieves comparable efficiency to LoRA while outperforming full fine-tuning across multiple settings.

items.title: The Readout Shortcut: Positional Number Copying Dominates Arithmetic CoT Readout in Small Language Models
items.summary: Small language models rely on chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting for arithmetic tasks. The model's performance can be dominated by a positional shortcut, where it copies the number at the end of the input before the answer delimiter, regardless of intermediate reasoning, accounting for 54-92 pp of accuracy. This copy channel takes precedence over retained-context completion and is observed in three models on GSM8K. Removing this shortcut recovers accuracy on arithmetic tasks.

items.title: Approximate Machine Unlearning through Manifold Representation Forgetting Guided by Self Mode Connectivity
items.summary: Approximate machine unlearning is a mechanism that enforces the right to be forgotten, but existing methods often deliver limited results and undermine original learning objectives. A new approach called ManiF-SMC reformulates unlearning as pushing erased samples away from their original manifold representation centroid toward nearest neighbors in retained data. ManiF-SMC aligns unlearning with retraining behavior using a margin-based triplet loss and a self-mode-connectivity module to guide adaptive margins generation. It achieves comparable unlearning effectiveness to state-of-the-art methods while operating within the model's representation space.

items.title: MedExpMem: Adapting Experience Memory for Differential Diagnosis
items.summary: MedExpMem is an experience memory framework enabling VLM-based diagnostic agents to accumulate differential diagnosis expertise by memorizing discriminative experiences derived from diagnostic failures. The framework mirrors physician learning through two phases: initial practice and reflective re-diagnosis, guiding differential reasoning when encountering new cases. Results show consistent accuracy improvements of up to 7.0% across diverse models and scales on a radiology benchmark spanning 11 subspecialties. MedExpMem addresses medical adaptation needs beyond the reach of parameteric learning, demonstrating robustness and competitive performance in analytical experiments.

items.title: When Do LLMs Reason? A Dynamical Systems View via Entropy Phase Transitions
items.summary: LLMs' reasoning is not a static property, but rather an emergent dynamic state during generation. Early-stage entropy dynamics provide a signal of this state, with tasks benefiting from CoT exhibiting consistent entropy reduction. A proposed framework, EDRM, leverages early decoding entropy to adaptively select inference strategies, consistently outperforming static baselines across 15 benchmarks and 4 LLMs.

items.title: WeCon: An Efficient Weight-Conditioned Neural Solver for Multi-Objective Combinatorial Optimization Problems
items.summary: Existing neural solvers for Multi-Objective Combinatorial Optimization Problems often use decomposition-based strategies with limited weight-conditioned context modeling. The proposed Weight-Conditioned neural solver (WeCon) addresses this limitation by introducing an encoder layer and Gated Residual Fusion block to facilitate informative weight-conditioned context, reducing weight-signal dilution in the decoder using a plug-and-play Residual Fusion block. Efficient Preference Optimization is also introduced to construct high-quality solutions, leading to improved training effectiveness. WeCon achieves comparable HyperVolume values to SOTA solver POCCO-W while reducing inference time by 40%.

items.title: Tensor Cache: Eviction-conditioned Associative Memory for Transformers
items.summary: Autoregressive Transformer KV caches grow linearly with context length, but sliding-window caching discards evicted tokens entirely. A two-level cache is introduced: a first-level cache (L1) using sliding-window softmax attention and a second-level cache (L2) using a fixed-size outer-product fast-weight memory fed by evicted KV pairs. The L2 cache reads evicted pairs through matrix multiplication, improving memory-quality frontier over bounded-state baselines.

items.title: Diffusion-based Denoising Beats Vanilla Score Matching in Parameter Estimation: A Theoretical Explanation
items.summary: Score matching is an alternative to maximum likelihood estimation for multimodal distributions. Vanilla score matching has shown to be inefficient relative to maximum likelihood estimation for well-separated modes. A new diffusion-based denoising score matching estimator (DDSME) provides statistical guarantees and improves upon the vanilla SME, avoiding error bound worsening with increasing mode separation through suitable hyperparameter tuning.

items.title: KAPLAN: Kolmogorov-Arnold Prognostic Learnable Activation Networks for Survival Analysis
items.summary: KAPLAN-HR is a B-spline Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN) model for nonparametric estimation of conditional hazard in survival analysis, allowing joint modeling of covariates and time without manually specified interactions and time-varying effects. A single-layer KAPLAN-HR model recovers a generalized additive model, while deeper architectures capture interactions and time-varying effects. The convergence rate of the nonparametric KAN hazard estimator depends only on the smoothness of the underlying KAN representation, mitigating the curse of dimensionality. KAPLAN-HR outperforms established statistical and deep learning survival methods in six clinical benchmark datasets.

items.title: LLM Sparsity Prior for Robust Feature Selection
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are sensitive to weight quality when used for high-dimensional variable selection, degrading performance with inaccurate weights. A new framework quantifies LLM-generated weight quality, allowing rigorous evaluation of LLM-informed methods. The LLM Sparsity Prior (LSP) integrates LLM weights into prior inclusion probabilities using two interpretable hyperparameters, improving robustness without sacrificing gains when weights are accurate.

items.title: Operationalizing Individual Fairness via Gradient Descent and Bradley-Terry Models
items.summary: Individual fairness ensures that "similar individuals should be treated similarly" in algorithmic decision-making. A barrier is learning a similarity metric over individuals, but an algorithm was developed to address this by using gradient descent with a spectral initialization step. The algorithm converges quickly to the ground truth metric despite non-convexity of the loss function. It also provides fairness guarantees and can be used for AI model tuning.

items.title: Coupled Training with Privileged Information and Unlabeled Data
items.summary: A common strategy in prediction problems involves first training a model with all available information and then using its predictions to train another model only using inputs available at test time, but this approach can be flawed if the extra information is weak or noisy. To address this issue, researchers propose a joint training method that learns two models together, allowing the deployment model to benefit from additional information without inheriting mistakes. This approach provides guarantees for when it improves prediction accuracy and analyzes an alternating training algorithm for large, high-dimensional models. Experiments show that this approach robustly outperforms standard Two-Stage baselines.

items.title: Concomitant DAG Learning: On the Roles of Noise Adaptivity, Sparsity, and Non-negativity
items.summary: Directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) model cause-effect interactions but inferring DAGs from observational data poses challenges due to unknown causal structures and infeasible interventions. Recent signal processing advances address these issues by recasting DAG structure learning as a continuous score-based estimation problem over adjacency matrices. Concomitant DAG estimation methods jointly infer sparse causal structure and exogenous noise levels, improving robustness under heteroscedasticity and distribution shifts. This tutorial introduces emerging directions including online, nonlinear, and neural causal discovery.

items.title: Asymmetric Scaling Laws from Sparse Features
items.summary: A new model introduces asymptotic population loss laws with sparse activations, showing a double-descent peak near interpolation threshold and distinct scaling exponents in overparameterized and underparameterized regimes. The gap between these exponents is determined by the degree of sparsity. A compute-optimal frontier favors increasing dataset size over model capacity under fixed budgets. Gradient-descent dynamics exhibit a specific scaling law for instability, unaffected by nonlinear activations.

items.title: Dirichlet-Based Monte Carlo Dropout for Uncertainty Estimation in Neural Networks
items.summary: MC Dropout has been enhanced to estimate uncertainty using a Dirichlet-based framework within the formulation by Sensoy et al. (2018), which models class probabilities using a Dirichlet distribution. This approach maintains computational efficiency while improving the quality of uncertainty estimates. The proposed method produces well-calibrated uncertainty estimates, offering a practical solution for uncertainty-aware deep learning models. It is compared with existing uncertainty quantification techniques.

items.title: Learning Kernel-Based MDPs from Episodic Preferential Feedback
items.summary: Human feedback often arrives as preferences rather than calibrated numeric rewards, motivating reinforcement learning from preferential feedback. Researchers developed a rigorous study on preference-only learning in episodic kernel MDPs and created preference-based value estimation and confidence sets. The study proves high-probability regret bounds that scale sublinearly in the number of episodes, implying the learned policy's value converges to the optimal policy's value.

items.title: Move on Muon : A Hamiltonian probability gradient flow perspective of Muon optimizer
items.summary: Gradient flow is used on the space of probability measures defined on matrix-valued parameters induced by regularized Muon optimizer. The regularized orthogonalization map is identified as the gradient of a smooth Fenchel-dual smoothing of the nuclear norm, allowing for lifting to finite-particle probability objectives. The resulting flow is shown to be a damped Hamiltonian probability dynamics whose kinetic energy is induced by the regularized Muon mirror potential.

items.title: Remote Teleoperation of Endovascular Intervention Robots: A Systematic Review
items.summary: Remote robotic-assisted endovascular intervention reduces clinician radiation exposure and physical strain while extending specialized vascular care to geographically distant regions. Studies found that teleoperated catheters can navigate distances up to 7000 km with robust communication infrastructure, and initial outcomes showed high procedural success in small-scale human trials. However, most evidence came from animal or phantom models, highlighting the need for multi-center clinical trials to validate safety and efficacy.

items.title: Extending Deep Event Visual Odometry with Sparse Point-Cloud Export
items.summary: Deep Event Visual Odometry (DEVO) extends monocular event-only odometry by combining patch tracking, learned patch selection, recurrent correspondence refinement, and differentiable bundle adjustment. A sparse point-cloud export pipeline is added to preserve the original visual odometry pipeline while enabling geometric scene output. The resulting system achieves high precision at a 5 cm threshold on the BOARD SLOW sequence, with locally consistent results matching EMVS reconstructions.

items.title: Agentic-VLA: Efficient Online Adaptation for Vision-Language-Action Models
items.summary: VLA models leverage pre-trained vision-language representations for robotic manipulation. A new training framework called Agentic-VLA overcomes limitations by dynamically generating reward functions, providing structured exploration guidance, and storing task-relevant policy weights. Agentic-VLA achieves substantial improvements on the LIBERO benchmark and RoboTwin 2.0 benchmark, including faster convergence.

items.title: Robots That Know What to Ask: Recovering Misaligned Rewards through Targeted Explanations
items.summary: Learning reward functions from demonstrations often relies on perfect supervision of all features, but demonstrations can be imperfect due to cognitive load or physical difficulty. To address this, a framework is proposed that detects underspecified features and solicits targeted corrective demonstrations. Demonstrations implicitly reveal which features are well-specified by showing little variation, while underspecified features vary widely. The robot then queries for demonstrations to explicitly address the identified gaps, significantly improving reward recovery in simulated and real-world tests.

items.title: Verified Task-Space Motion Planning Under Joint-Space Constraints
items.summary: Reactive task-space planners like Bug2 operate with fixed Cartesian step sizes, unaware of joint-angle limits. This can cause tracking drift and prevent goal-reaching when Jacobian conditions are poorly met. A new planner addresses this by computing a certified reachable hyperrectangle under joint displacement bounds, adapting its step size to local kinematic conditioning. The new planner achieves zero joint-limit violations and a 100% goal-reaching rate in statistical evaluations.

items.title: PIMbot: A Self-Adaptive Attack Framework for Adversarial Manipulation of Multi-Robot Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Researchers have developed PIMbot, a self-adaptive attack framework for manipulating outcomes in multi-robot reinforcement learning. It utilizes two complementary levers: incentive manipulation of the reward channel and policy manipulation of an agent's actions. An adaptive controller balances these levers online to achieve desired outcomes. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of PIMbot in both simulated and real-world environments, showcasing its potential as a stress-test tool for multi-robot cooperative tasks.

items.title: UfM*: Uncertainty from Motion* for DNN Depth Estimation Using Gaussians
items.summary: UfM* is an uncertainty estimation algorithm for monocular depth DNNs in safety-critical robotic systems. It measures multiview disagreement efficiently by comparing previous and current views using a compact Gaussian mixture, requiring only one DNN inference per image. UfM* paired with aleatoric uncertainty improves expected calibration error by 24-28% compared to an ensemble. It requires significantly less energy (63 mJ) and memory than previous approaches, enabling efficient uncertainty estimation for resource-constrained robotic systems.

items.title: Four Simple Proprioceptive Estimators for Legged Robots
items.summary: Legged robots utilize an IMU that experiences solution drift due to noise. The feet' intermittent contacts with the environment can be used to mitigate this drift by leveraging them in state estimators. A sequence of four estimators is developed, starting from a contact-aided invariant EKF and progressing to a fixed-lag smoother.

items.title: $\pi_0$-EqM: Equilibrium Matching for Closed-Loop Vision-Language-Action Control
items.summary: $\pi_0$-EqM improves RoboTwin's average success from 40.4% to 50.2% across 19 tasks, outperforming the baseline under a matched 300-step budget. The results also show a task-dependent non-monotonic relation between residual and success, known as the stationarity-executability gap. $\pi_0$-EqM remains competitive on LIBERO, with its clearest gain on LIBERO-10 (87.0%).

items.title: Semantic-Aware Guided Drone Exploration for Language-Conditioned 3D Indoor Mapping
items.summary: SAGE (Semantic-Aware Guided Exploration) is a system for open-vocabulary exploration in unknown 3D indoor environments that incorporates Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training (CLIP). It integrates CLIP via four key components and outperforms FALCON and a semantic-only ablation in object discovery across map-query pairs. SAGE achieves faster completion times, higher volumetric throughput, and superior object discovery compared to Finding Things in the Unknown (FTU), with a mean speedup of 13.7.
